transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I guess... I mean, I'm a hairstylist, you know? And usually, I'm pretty quick on my feet. I have to be. You get a client in the chair, you talk to them, you figure out what they want, and you just go. But lately... I don't know, it's just been really hard. It's like my hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. I don't even know how else to describe it. Like, even just sectioning hair, which I’ve done a million times and usually takes me two seconds, or mixing color in the back room—it takes me forever now. It's like my brain is telling my hands to move, but they just won't cooperate the way they're supposed to. And the worst part is, people have started noticing. My manager pulled me aside the other day and asked if I was feeling okay because I was falling behind on my appointments, and I'm just slower than I used to be. I try to speed up, I really do, but it's like I'm physically weighed down or something, and I just can't shake it off no matter how much coffee I drink or how hard I try to focus. It's really starting to mess with my job, and I just... I don't know what's wrong with me.
Have you noticed this slowness in movement or feeling weighed down only at work, or has it been happening in other parts of your life too, like at home or when doing everyday tasks?

Well, I mean, like I was just saying about work... it's definitely the most obvious there, or at least that's where it causes the most problems. Because, you know, at the salon you're on a really strict schedule, and like I mentioned, my hands literally just feel like they’re dragging through thick, heavy glue. Even the most basic stuff, like sectioning hair for a blowout or standing in the back room mixing the developer and the color... it just takes me forever now. And having my manager and the other stylists actually noticing that I'm just way slower than I used to be... that's the part that really gets to me, it's so embarrassing. 

But to answer your question... yeah, it's happening at home, too. It's everywhere. It's just that at home, nobody is standing over my shoulder timing me, right? Like, getting ready in the morning has become this whole exhausting ordeal. I’ll sit on the edge of my bed holding a sock for what feels like twenty minutes, or I'll be doing my own makeup—which I usually love, it's my me-time, you know?—and just lifting the mascara wand to my eye makes my arm feel like it weighs a hundred pounds. It takes me twice as long just to get out the door to even get to the salon. 

But my mind always goes right back to work, because that's where I can't hide it. I can't just pause a client's haircut or take a break in the middle of applying foils because my hands won't cooperate. I just keep trying to push through the heaviness, but I can't, and I just end up apologizing to them for taking so long. I really hate it.

Have you noticed that your speech has also slowed down or that you're moving much slower than usual even when you're not trying to do something specific, like talking to friends or walking across a room?

Well, like I was saying before, it's really the physical stuff that I notice the most, especially with my hands. I know you're asking about talking or walking, but honestly, my mind just keeps going back to how my hands feel like they’re moving through glue at work. It's just so frustrating because I'm a hairstylist, and my hands are my livelihood, you know? Like, even sectioning hair, which is something I do without even thinking, or mixing color in the back room—it takes me forever now. I'll be standing there with the bowl and the brush, and it's like my arm is just refusing to move at a normal speed. 

And the thing that really gets to me, the thing that makes it so much worse than just being tired, is that people have started noticing that I’m just slower than I used to be. My manager, my clients... they can see it. So, I mean, maybe my walking is slower? I guess it takes me longer to walk from the breakroom to my station, but I'm so hyper-focused on how heavy and slow my arms and hands are when I'm actually trying to do my job that it's hard to think about anything else. I just feel like I'm letting everyone down because I can't move the way I'm supposed to, and no matter how much I try to force it, my hands just feel like they're dragging through mud.
Have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, like doing your own makeup or anything else, even when it's not related to work?

Well, I guess... I mean, you mentioned my makeup, and like I said, that used to be my me-time. I used to really enjoy it. But lately, it's just... I don't know, it's not just the heaviness, it's like the whole feeling behind it is gone. And it's not just the makeup. It's kind of everything. Like, at work, I used to be the one who was always chatting with my clients, you know? I’d ask about their kids, their vacations, we’d laugh, I’d really get into it. I’d even go out of my way to help the newer stylists if they were struggling with a tricky color correction or a new cutting technique. I loved doing that, being the experienced one they could come to. 

But now? I just... I don't have that spark in me anymore. I literally just keep my head down. I do the hair, I barely say a word unless I have to, and I just try to get through it without anyone talking to me. It's like my personality has just been drained out of me. And it's not just at the salon, either. I used to love being outdoors. I have this group of friends, and we used to go hiking almost every weekend. We’d pick a new trail, pack a lunch, and just spend hours out there talking and exploring. I haven't gone with them in months. They text me, they invite me, and I just make up excuses or ignore it entirely. I avoid them, honestly. I avoid most people now. I just don't have the energy or the... the desire to engage with anyone or anything. It's like the color has been sucked out of everything I used to like doing, and I just feel so flat and empty inside. I just want to be left alone, which is so unlike me, but I just can't find that part of myself that used to care about those things.
Have you been feeling like you're a failure or that you're letting people down, even when there's no real reason to feel that way?

Yeah... yeah, I do. All the time. I mean, you said "when there's no real reason," but to me, it feels like there are a million reasons, you know? Like, I just keep thinking I’m this massive burden on everyone around me. My manager, my coworkers, my friends... even my clients. I just feel like I'm dragging everyone down with me. And the worst part is, I feel like I completely deserve this. Like, whatever this heavy, awful feeling is, I brought it on myself because I just couldn't keep my life together. 

I mean, I look back at how things used to be, and I just feel so incredibly guilty. I couldn't keep my money straight—I was always dipping into my savings because I'd call out of work when I couldn't get out of bed, and then my paychecks would be short. And then my job... I mean, I'm barely hanging on at the salon as it is. I can't even handle basic salon responsibilities anymore. Like, sweeping the floor around my chair or folding the towels when they come out of the dryer—things that take two seconds and that I used to do without thinking—now I just leave them, and someone else has to pick up my slack. I see the other girls doing it, and I just feel this crushing weight of guilt, like I'm just this useless person taking up space. 

It's just this constant loop in my head telling me that I'm failing at everything. I'm failing as a stylist, I'm failing as a friend, I'm failing as an adult. I should be able to just go to work and do my job and be normal, but I can't. And because I can't, I just feel like I deserve to feel this miserable. I deserve to lose my clients, I deserve to be broke, because I'm just not trying hard enough, even though I feel like I'm trying with everything I have. It's just... it's exhausting feeling this guilty and worthless all the time. I just feel like everyone would be better off if they didn't have to deal with me and my mess.
Have you felt a loss of energy or noticed that you get tired much more easily, even when you're not doing anything physically demanding?

I mean... no, not really? It’s kind of hard to explain because I know I just said I feel heavy and I don't want to do anything, but it’s not really about being *tired*, if that makes sense. Like, I don't feel physically exhausted in the way you're asking about. People always assume I'm just worn out because I work on my feet all day at the salon, and yeah, being a hairstylist is physically demanding—you're standing, you're holding your arms up at weird angles, you're constantly moving around the chair. But my body itself, my muscles... they don't actually feel tired. I don't feel like I need to take a nap or like I'm running out of physical energy. 

It's more like... I just don't have the will to use the energy I do have. Like I said before, I'll call out of work and just stay in bed, but I'm not sleeping. I'm not lying there because I'm so fatigued I can't keep my eyes open. I'm usually just lying there wide awake, staring at the ceiling, just completely consumed by all that guilt and that feeling of being a failure that I was telling you about. My mind is just spinning with how much I'm messing everything up. 

So, if I'm not doing anything physically demanding, like if I'm just sitting on the couch on my day off, I don't feel like my energy is drained. I just feel... stuck. Like the energy is there somewhere, but it's trapped under all that mud and glue I was talking about with my hands. I'm just so hyper-focused on how awful I feel about myself that I just don't move. So, no, I wouldn't say I get tired more easily or have a loss of energy. It's really just the heaviness and the total lack of wanting to participate in my own life, rather than actually being out of energy, you know?
Have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

Yeah... honestly, yes. It’s been going on for way longer than two weeks, but definitely every single day lately. It's just this constant, overwhelming feeling. 

Almost every single day, I wake up, and before I even really open my eyes or look at my phone, I just feel this... this heavy, flat sadness right here in my chest. It just sits there, like a physical weight pressing down on me. And the moment I feel it, my brain just immediately goes to this place of... well, what is the point? It just feels like there is absolutely no point in trying to build the life I was planning. 

I used to have all these big plans, you know? I got my associate's degree, I got my cosmetology license, and I had this whole timeline mapped out in my head. I was going to build up this massive, loyal clientele, and then in a couple of years, I was going to rent my own studio suite, and maybe one day even open a full salon of my own. I had vision boards, I had Pinterest folders full of salon decor and branding ideas, I had all these goals for my future. But now? Now I wake up with that awful, heavy feeling in my chest, and I look at all those dreams and I just think, why even bother? It's all just completely pointless. 

It’s not just a passing morning mood, either. It’s like this thick, dark fog that just hangs over me for the entire day. From the minute my alarm goes off, I'm just dreading having to exist and go through the motions. I try to talk myself out of it, I really do. I'll lie there staring at the ceiling and tell myself, 'Okay, just get up, just make some coffee, just go be normal,' but that flat sadness just doesn't budge. It's so discouraging. It makes me feel completely hopeless about my future, because if I can't even get out of bed without feeling like my heart is made of lead, how am I ever going to achieve any of the things I wanted to do? How am I supposed to run a business or be successful when I feel this empty all the time? So yeah, most of the day, every single day, I just feel completely defeated and down. It never really goes away.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

Yeah... yeah, I definitely have. It’s actually been kind of noticeable lately, but not because I’m, like, trying to diet or anything like that. I just... I’ve been skipping meals without really meaning to. 

It’s like, I wake up with that heavy feeling I was telling you about, and the absolute last thing on my mind is breakfast. I’ll usually just make a coffee, you know, just to try and force myself to get out the door. And then I get to the salon, and usually, the girls and I would order lunch together or someone would run out to grab sandwiches between clients. But lately, I just... I don't even think about food. Even when I have a gap in my schedule, or when I'm just hiding in the break room because I can't face the floor, I don't eat. I'll just sit there. And it’s not even that I’m purposefully starving myself, it’s just that the thought of eating feels like too much work. Like, chewing and swallowing just feels exhausting, and nothing sounds good anyway. 

So the whole day will go by, and I’ll finally get home at night, and I’ll be sitting on my couch—just stuck there, like I said before, completely trapped in my own head—and it’ll suddenly hit me. I'll realize it's, like, nine o'clock at night and all I’ve had the entire day was that one coffee in the morning and maybe, I don't know, a few bites of a granola bar that I found in the bottom of my purse before I couldn't stomach the rest of it. It’s just wild how you can completely forget to do the most basic human thing, like feeding yourself. It just makes me feel even more broken, to be honest.

And because it's been happening so much, my clothes have definitely gotten looser. I have this one pair of black jeans that are my absolute favorite to wear behind the chair—they used to fit perfectly, really snug and professional-looking. But now they’re just sagging on me. I'm having to pull them up all day, or I have to wear a belt pulled to the tightest notch, and even my work apron feels like it's just hanging off my shoulders differently. It’s embarrassing, really. I feel like my coworkers must be looking at me and seeing how baggy my clothes are getting, and it just adds to this whole feeling that I'm completely falling apart and everyone can see it. So, yeah, I've definitely been losing weight without trying, just because I can't seem to remember to eat.

And the worst part is, I feel like I completely deserve this. Like, whatever this heavy, awful feeling is, I brought it on myself because I just couldn't keep my life together.

I couldn't keep my money straight—I was always dipping into my savings because I'd call out of work when I couldn't get out of bed, and then my paychecks would be short. And then my job... I mean, I'm barely hanging on at the salon as it is. I can't even handle basic salon responsibilities anymore. Like, sweeping the floor around my chair or folding the towels when they come out of the dryer—things that take two seconds and that I used to do without thinking—now I just leave them, and someone else has to pick up my slack. I see the other girls doing it, and I just feel this crushing weight of guilt, like I'm just this useless person taking up space. 

It's just this constant loop in my head telling me that I'm failing at everything. I'm failing as a stylist, I'm failing as a friend, I'm failing as an adult. I should be able to just go to work and do my job and be normal, but I can't. And because I can't, I just feel like I deserve to feel this miserable. I deserve to lose my clients, I deserve to be broke, because I'm just not trying hard enough, even though I feel like I'm trying with everything I have. It's just... it's exhausting feeling this guilty and worthless all the time. I just feel like everyone would be better off if they didn't have to deal with me and my mess.

I'm usually just lying there wide awake, staring at the ceiling, just completely consumed by all that guilt and that feeling of being a failure that I was telling you about. My mind is just spinning with how much I'm messing everything up. 

So, if I'm not doing anything physically demanding, like if I'm just sitting on the couch on my day off, I don't feel like my energy is drained. I just feel... stuck. Like the energy is there somewhere, but it's trapped under all that mud and glue I was talking about with my hands. I'm just so hyper-focused on how awful I feel about myself that I just don't move. So, no, I wouldn't say I get tired more easily or have a loss of energy. It's really just the heaviness and the total lack of wanting to participate in my own life, rather than actually being out of energy, you know?

inference.note: The patient denies a loss of energy or increased fatigue, which reduces the likelihood of F32.2 and F33.2, where fatigue is a key criterion. The presence of psychomotor slowing, anhedonia, feelings of worthlessness, and guilt supports the continuation of the severe episode codes (F32.3 and F33.3).

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day, as a key differentiator between major depressive disorder (F32.3) and persistent depressive disorder (F33.3).
doctor.question: Have you felt down, depressed, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for at least the past two weeks?

target_item.name: Depressed_Mood
target_item.manifestation: Most days I wake up with this heavy, flat sadness in my chest, like there’s no point in trying to build the life I was planning.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about feeling down, depressed, or hopeless, which directly corresponds to the Depressed Mood symptom in my profile.

patient.answer:
Yeah... honestly, yes. It’s been going on for way longer than two weeks, but definitely every single day lately. It's just this constant, overwhelming feeling. 

Almost every single day, I wake up, and before I even really open my eyes or look at my phone, I just feel this... this heavy, flat sadness right here in my chest. It just sits there, like a physical weight pressing down on me. And the moment I feel it, my brain just immediately goes to this place of... well, what is the point? It just feels like there is absolutely no point in trying to build the life I was planning. 

I used to have all these big plans, you know? I got my associate's degree, I got my cosmetology license, and I had this whole timeline mapped out in my head. I was going to build up this massive, loyal clientele, and then in a couple of years, I was going to rent my own studio suite, and maybe one day even open a full salon of my own. I had vision boards, I had Pinterest folders full of salon decor and branding ideas, I had all these goals for my future. But now? Now I wake up with that awful, heavy feeling in my chest, and I look at all those dreams and I just think, why even bother? It's all just completely pointless. 

It’s not just a passing morning mood, either. It’s like this thick, dark fog that just hangs over me for the entire day. From the minute my alarm goes off, I'm just dreading having to exist and go through the motions. I try to talk myself out of it, I really do. I'll lie there staring at the ceiling and tell myself, 'Okay, just get up, just make some coffee, just go be normal,' but that flat sadness just doesn't budge. It's so discouraging. It makes me feel completely hopeless about my future, because if I can't even get out of bed without feeling like my heart is made of lead, how am I ever going to achieve any of the things I wanted to do? How am I supposed to run a business or be successful when I feel this empty all the time? So yeah, most of the day, every single day, I just feel completely defeated and down. It never really goes away.

inference.note: The patient endorsed feeling down, depressed, and hopeless most of the day, nearly every day, for longer than two weeks, which supports the continuation of F32.3 (Major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe) and F33.3 (Major depressive disorder, recurrent, severe) as differential candidates. No features of bipolar disorder or psychotic features were endorsed, and the presentation remains consistent with severe unipolar depression, either as a single episode or recurrent course. The distinction between F32.3 and F33.3 remains uncertain without more clarity on the duration and recurrence of episodes.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient has experienced a significant change in appetite or weight as part of their depressive episode, which helps confirm the diagnosis of a major depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently—like eating a lot less or more than usual, or losing or gaining weight without trying?

target_item.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
target_item.manifestation: I’ve been skipping meals without really meaning to, then realizing at night I only had coffee and a few bites of something, and my clothes have gotten looser.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about significant changes in appetite or weight, which directly corresponds to my symptom of skipping meals and losing weight.

patient.answer:
Yeah... yeah, I definitely have. It’s actually been kind of noticeable lately, but not because I’m, like, trying to diet or anything like that. I just... I’ve been skipping meals without really meaning to. 

It’s like, I wake up with that heavy feeling I was telling you about, and the absolute last thing on my mind is breakfast. I’ll usually just make a coffee, you know, just to try and force myself to get out the door. And then I get to the salon, and usually, the girls and I would order lunch together or someone would run out to grab sandwiches between clients. But lately, I just... I don't even think about food. Even when I have a gap in my schedule, or when I'm just hiding in the break room because I can't face the floor, I don't eat. I'll just sit there. And it’s not even that I’m purposefully starving myself, it’s just that the thought of eating feels like too much work. Like, chewing and swallowing just feels exhausting, and nothing sounds good anyway. 

So the whole day will go by, and I’ll finally get home at night, and I’ll be sitting on my couch—just stuck there, like I said before, completely trapped in my own head—and it’ll suddenly hit me. I'll realize it's, like, nine o'clock at night and all I’ve had the entire day was that one coffee in the morning and maybe, I don't know, a few bites of a granola bar that I found in the bottom of my purse before I couldn't stomach the rest of it. It’s just wild how you can completely forget to do the most basic human thing, like feeding yourself. It just makes me feel even more broken, to be honest.

And because it's been happening so much, my clothes have definitely gotten looser. I have this one pair of black jeans that are my absolute favorite to wear behind the chair—they used to fit perfectly, really snug and professional-looking. But now they’re just sagging on me. I'm having to pull them up all day, or I have to wear a belt pulled to the tightest notch, and even my work apron feels like it's just hanging off my shoulders differently. It’s embarrassing, really. I feel like my coworkers must be looking at me and seeing how baggy my clothes are getting, and it just adds to this whole feeling that I'm completely falling apart and everyone can see it. So, yeah, I've definitely been losing weight without trying, just because I can't seem to remember to eat.
